t.1.11.1: Then, after a long time had passed, when a certain most delightful spring had arrived, the king's mind turned to performing a sacrifice.
t.1.11.2: Then, having won the favour of that brahmin of godlike complexion by bowing his head, he chose him for the sacrifice and for the continuation of his lineage.
t.1.11.3: Saying “So be it,” he, highly honored, spoke to the king: “Let those requisites be gathered, and let the horse be set free.”
t.1.11.4: Then the king spoke these words to Sumantra, the best of ministers: "Sumantra, quickly summon the officiating priests who are expounders of the Veda."
t.1.11.5: Then Sumantra, swift in his stride, went quickly and brought together all those brahmins who had mastered the Vedas.
t.1.11.7: Then, having honored them, the righteous-souled King Daśaratha spoke these gentle words, endowed with dharma and artha.
t.1.11.6: Suyajña and Vāmadeva, Jābāli and Kāśyapa, and the family priest Vasiṣṭha, along with those others who were the most excellent of the twice-born.
t.1.11.8: For me, who keep lamenting for the sake of a son, there is truly no happiness. Therefore my resolve is this: for that purpose I shall perform the horse sacrifice.
t.1.11.9: Therefore I wish to perform a sacrifice by the rite prescribed in the scriptures, and through the power of the sage's son I too shall attain my desires.
t.1.11.10: Then all the brāhmaṇas, headed by Vasiṣṭha, honored with "Excellent!" that speech which had fallen from the mouth of the king.
t.1.11.11: Then those led by Ṛṣyaśṛṅga replied to the king: "Let those materials be gathered, and let the horse be set free."
t.1.11.13: Then, having heard those words of the twice-born, the king was pleased, and with joy the king spoke these auspicious words to his ministers.
t.1.11.15: Let the ground for the sacrifice be prepared on the northern bank of the Sarayū, and let the propitiatory rites be performed abundantly, according to precept and according to rule.
t.1.11.14: At the word of the elders, let my materials for the sacrifice be quickly gathered, and let the horse, guarded by capable men and accompanied by the preceptor, be set free.
t.1.11.16: This sacrifice can indeed be performed by any king, provided that no grievous fault occurs in this most excellent of rites.
t.1.11.17: For learned brahmarākṣasas seek out a flaw here; the performer of a sacrifice lacking the proper rites perishes at once.
t.1.11.18: So let everything be so arranged that this sacrifice of mine is first brought to completion according to the prescribed rule; you who are here are capable in the performance of the rites.
t.1.11.19: Then all the ministers, saying "So be it," received with honour those words of the lord of kings, and they did just as they had been commanded.
t.1.11.12: In every way you shall obtain four sons of boundless valor, you in whom this righteous resolve has arisen for the sake of sons.
t.1.11.20: Then those twice-born praised that bull among kings, the knower of dharma; and then, having been given leave, they all went back again the way they had come.
t.1.11.21: When the twice-born had departed, the lord of men, of great splendor, dismissed those ministers and entered his own palace.
